prompt: How much did each 2025 promotion lift unit sales? For each promotion that started in 2025 (start_date from 1 January to 31 December 2025), give uplift_units, the units sold on promotion minus the baseline units, and uplift_pct, that difference as a percentage of the baseline units, rounded to 1 decimal with ROUND (12.5 for 12.5%). A sales line is on a promotion when it carries that promotion's ID in order_lines.promo_id, whatever its date; where two promotions overlap on a product, a line carries only the deeper one, so it counts once. The baseline ends the day before the promotion's start_date and has as many days as the promotion ran, start_date and end_date both counted; it holds every sales line of the promotion's products in those days, whatever promotion the line carries. Days are sales.order_date, the UTC day of the order. A period with no sale counts 0 units, and uplift_pct is missing when the baseline has no units. Return three columns, in this order: promo_id, uplift_units and uplift_pct. Return one row for each such promotion. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per promotion that started in 2025

hints: Next, write the same-length baseline window, then subtract the baseline from the promotion's units.
The percentage divides the difference by the baseline; a promotion whose baseline is missing gets a missing percentage.
faded_shape:
WITH promo AS (
  -- one row per promotion that started in 2025
  SELECT promo_id, start_date, end_date - start_date + 1 AS days
  FROM promotions
  WHERE start_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
), during AS (
  -- one row per promotion that started in 2025
  SELECT p.promo_id, SUM(ol.quantity) AS units
  FROM promo p
  JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.promo_id = p.promo_id
  GROUP BY p.promo_id
), baseline AS (
  -- one row per promotion with a baseline sale
  SELECT p.promo_id, SUM(s.units) AS units
  FROM promo p
  JOIN promotion_products pp ON pp.promo_id = p.promo_id
  JOIN sales s ON s.product_id = pp.product_id
why_this_works: Uplift compares the promotion with a baseline of the same length, and dividing by the baseline turns the gain into a percentage.
faded_suffix:
GROUP BY p.promo_id
)
SELECT p.promo_id, COALESCE(d.units, 0) - COALESCE(b.units, 0) AS uplift_units,
  ROUND(100.0 * (COALESCE(d.units, 0) - b.units) / b.units, 1) AS uplift_pct
FROM promo p
LEFT JOIN during d ON d.promo_id = p.promo_id
LEFT JOIN baseline b ON b.promo_id = p.promo_id
